title: Twenty years on, the midterms rhymed
subject: politics
native_material: the Capitol, Senate seat counts, the flipped states, the 2006 precedent
hook_mechanism: the 2026 flip of both houses, echoed by the 2006 flip under the last Republican president to lose both

pick.owner_words: "now give sample video of 1 minutes on current indian politics and 1 minute video on american politics. lets see what we have learnt. again freehand." (the owner delegated the topic and the pick; reverse-autopsy excluded as the India film's engine)

concept.logline: In 2026 a Republican president lost both houses of Congress for the first time since 2006; the midterm swing repeated itself.
concept.claim: Democrats took both houses on 3 November 2026; the last time a Republican president lost both was Bush in 2006, and the president's party usually loses House seats at midterms.

thumbnail: Statement: Twenty years on, the midterms *rhymed*.

scenes.narration: November third, twenty twenty-six. Both houses of Congress flip.

scenes.narration: Democrats win the House and the Senate.

scenes.narration: Going in, Republicans held the Senate, fifty-three to forty-seven.

scenes.narration: Control takes fifty-one. Democrats passed it.

scenes.narration: They flipped seats in Texas, Kansas, Iowa, South Carolina and Maine.
scenes.graphic: Heatmap: Texas 1, Kansas 1, Iowa 1, South Carolina 1, Maine 1 | Senate seats Democrats flipped | seats, 2026

scenes.narration: Kansas had not elected a Democratic senator since 1932.
scenes.graphic: Hero: wheat + ballot box | KANSAS | Democrat · Senate | first since 1932

scenes.narration: We have seen this before. The last Republican president to lose both houses: George W. Bush, in two thousand six.
scenes.graphic: Compare: person:George W. Bush + person:Donald Trump | 2006 | 2026 | Lost both houses of Congress

scenes.narration: That year, Republicans fell from 232 House seats to 202.

scenes.narration: Twenty years apart, the same swing.

scenes.narration: By Al Jazeera's count, the president's party lost House seats in eighteen of twenty midterms since 1946.
About a hundred and twenty-four million people voted, by a preliminary count.
